title: Brunswick Stew
subtitle: American Southern smoky chicken and vegetable stew
excerpt: The hearty, smoky stew of the American South: pulled chicken in a thick tomato base with sweetcorn, butter beans, and a barbecue-style tang from Worcestershire sauce and a little vinegar. A dish built to feed a crowd from a single pot.

recipe.sourceNotes: Brunswick stew is a thick, substantial stew of the American South, claimed simultaneously by Brunswick County in Virginia and Brunswick, Georgia, both of which maintain that their version is the original. The earliest versions used squirrel or rabbit, the abundant game of the Southern forest, but chicken became the standard meat as the dish spread. Today it is closely associated with barbecue; many BBQ restaurants in Virginia and North Carolina serve it as a side dish alongside smoked pork, and it is often made from the leftover smoked meat trimmings. The defining characteristics are the thick tomato base, the combination of sweetcorn and butter beans or lima beans, the smoky flavour, and the sweet-sour-savoury profile from Worcestershire sauce, vinegar, and a little sugar. It should be thick enough that a spoon stood in the stew will almost stand on its own.

content.text: Simmer the stew uncovered for the final 30 minutes to let it thicken: it should be very dense, almost like a thick chilli. If the stew is too thin, keep cooking; if too thick, add a splash of stock or water. The flavour improves considerably over a day in the fridge.

items.preparation: bone-in; or 800 g leftover pulled chicken or smoked chicken
tinned, drained; or fresh kernels from 2 cobs
peeled and cut into 2 cm dice

content.text: If starting from raw chicken, simmer the thighs in the stock for 35 minutes until cooked. Remove, shred the meat, discard the skin and bones. Reserve the stock. Fry the onion in oil for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, smoked paprika, and cayenne and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tinned tomatoes, reserved stock, potato, Worcestershire sauce, vinegar, sugar, salt, and pepper. Bring to the boil and simmer for 25 minutes until the potato is tender.

Add the shredded chicken, sweetcorn, and butter beans. Simmer uncovered for 20 to 30 minutes until very thick. Taste and adjust the seasoning; it should be smoky, tangy, and sweet in balance. Serve in deep bowls with cornbread.
